titles.641: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — if Adam sinned loco nostro, why not also punished loco with corruption at once?
titles.642: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — mass-priest analogy: switching persons same moment (sin loco, punish suo)
titles.643: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — if punished loco with original-sin penalty, we should not receive the same
titles.644: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Christ parallel: loco punishment frees us; so Adam's loco original would free us too
titles.645: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'Adam sinned for us' leads to denying our original sin
titles.646: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — that denial can also be shown by the next argument (imputation vs inherent)

latin.641: Praeterea si loco nostro peccavit & peccatum illud merebatur poenam quae est peccatum, videlicet corruptionem: dic mihi, quaeso, cur non sit etiam loco nostro illa affectus poena? nam quo temporis articulo peccavit, eodem corruptus & vitiosus & iniustus factus est.
latin.642: Annon quo nomine peccavit eodem puniri debuit, praesertim eodem momento? nisi velis, quemadmodum sacrificulus pontificius inter celebrandum missam modo Christi personam induit, modo deponit, atque ita diversas agit personas eodem paene momento, sic Adamum similiter modo personam nostram repraesentasse, modo suam unius sustinuisse, atque eodem momento & peccasse loco nostro, & punitum suo, non nostro.
latin.643: Nam si loco nostro ea poena castigatus fuit quae est peccatum originale, non convenit nos eadem poena affici: quam enim loco nostro peccavit, tam loco nostro punitus est.
latin.644: Sicut enim quamvis ipsi in propriis nostris personis peccaverimus, tamen quia Christus loco nostro punitus est, non debemus amplius puniri: ita si pro illo peccato actuali punitus est Adamus loco nostro inflictione peccati originalis, non potest amplius pro eodem illo peccato nobis peccatum originale infligi.
latin.645: Vides quo te ducat tua ista assertio pro nobis peccasse Adamum: nimirum ad negandum peccatum nostrum originale.
latin.646: Quod ipsum etiam effici potest hoc argumento, ut videas magis magisque quam perniciosa sit illa sententia, a qua te dimovere cupio & conor.

pass_a.641: Placeus presses: if Adam sinned loco nostro and that act earned corruption as penalty, why wasn't he also hit with that penalty loco nostro? The instant he sinned he became corrupt, vicious, and unjust.
pass_a.642: Same title and same moment of punishment—unless you invent a mass-priest switch of persons: Adam representing us when sinning, sustaining only himself when punished, nearly at once. Placeus treats that costume-change as the only escape hatch.
pass_a.643: If the original-sin penalty already fell on Adam loco nostro, we should not also receive it—loco sin and loco punishment travel together.
pass_a.644: Christ-parallel cuts hard: we sin in our own persons yet need not be punished again because Christ was punished loco. So if Adam was already punished loco by having original sin inflicted for his actual sin, original cannot again be inflicted on us for that same act.
pass_a.645: Therefore Garrigues's assertion that Adam sinned for us drives straight toward denying that we have original sin of our own at all—that is where Placeus says the claim leads.
pass_a.646: Tip: Placeus will also prove that denial by the next argument, to show how pernicious the opinion is that he is trying to move Garrigues from. Tip before imputation-vs-inhaerentia.

641: Besides: if he sinned in our place, and that sin merited the penalty which is sin—namely corruption—tell me, I ask, why was he not also afflicted with that penalty in our place? For at the very moment he sinned, in the same he was made corrupt and vicious and unjust.
642: Ought he not to have been punished under the same title under which he sinned, especially at the same moment? Unless you mean that, as a pontifical priest celebrating mass puts on Christ's person and then puts it off, and so plays different persons in almost the same moment, so Adam likewise sometimes represented our person, sometimes sustained his own alone—and in the same moment both sinned in our place and was punished in his own, not ours.
643: For if he was chastised in our place with that penalty which is original sin, it does not fit that we should be afflicted with the same penalty: for as he sinned in our place, so he was punished in our place.
644: For just as, though we ourselves have sinned in our own persons, yet because Christ was punished in our place we ought not to be punished further: so if for that actual sin Adam was punished in our place by the infliction of original sin, original sin can no longer be inflicted on us for that same sin.
645: You see where that assertion of yours—that Adam sinned for us—leads you: namely to denying our original sin.
646: Which very thing can also be brought about by this argument, so that you may see more and more how pernicious that opinion is from which I desire and strive to move you.

642.gloss: punished in his own, not ours
